title: JESUS WEPT.
paragraphs:
Two words.
Three syllables.
And heaven’s heart breaks open.
Because in Gospel of John chapter 11, the Son of God stands in front of a tomb.

Not a metaphor.
Not a parable.
And inside it lies His friend—Lazarus of Bethany.

Mary of Bethany is collapsing in grief.
Martha of Bethany is fighting disappointment.

“Lord… if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”
(John 11:21)

The mourners are loud.
The air is thick with loss.
Four days in the tomb.
One moment that shakes theology to its bones.

Not a speech.
Not a sermon.

The Creator of tear ducts
lets them overflow.

Jesus already knows what He’s about to do.
In minutes, He will shout:
Brother, this is the heart of Christ.
Jesus does not stand distant from human pain.

He feels the ache of funerals.
He hears the sobbing of sisters.
He smells the rot of the grave.
God… standing in front of death…
The Gospel hidden in the tears
But this moment is bigger than Lazarus.
Because every tombstone on earth points forward to another grave.
One where Jesus Himself would lie.
that grave would explode with resurrection life.

The same Savior who wept at Lazarus’ tomb
would defeat the tomb forever.

If you’re staring at something that feels dead—
a dream, a relationship, a future—
Jesus is not cold toward your pain.
is the One who calls the dead to life.
And sometimes the miracle begins with tears.
